However, whether a 10-year Treasury note is a worthwhile investment highly depends on your savings goals, when you'll need access to your money, and your tolerance for the risk of selling if rates change. A high-yield savings account or money market account could be a better option for savers who value more flexibility and greater access to their cash, while a shorter-term CD can be a middle ground for savers who want the benefit of a fixed rate, but may not be willing to commit to a 10-year term or are fearful that locking into a Treasury note now could lock them out of higher returns if rates continue to increase.
